title: Really eBay? Every Sale is Via Promoted??? | Selling | eBay Community

facts.fact: eBay's Promoted Listings help page, as quoted by forum user mam98031, says the fee charged is based on the ad rate set for each listing.
facts.quote: The fee you are charged is based on the ad rate you set for each listing.

facts.fact: eBay's Promoted Listings help page, as quoted by forum user mam98031, defines an ad rate as a percentage of the item's total sale amount, including item price, shipping, taxes, and other applicable fees.
facts.quote: An ad rate is the percentage of an item's total sale amount (including item price, shipping, taxes, and any other applicable fees).

facts.fact: Forum user destinysdarlings2013 claims that in a hypothetical with a 5% promotion rate on a $27 item plus $3 sales tax, eBay would receive $1.50 because it calculates the fee on the $30 total. This is the user's claim, not an eBay statement.
facts.quote: they use the $30 figure so they would receive $1.50

facts.fact: Forum user yellow-snapdragon, a self-described hobby seller, says they sold close to 2,000 items organically over the years before starting to promote listings. This is an anecdotal seller claim.
facts.quote: have sold close to 2,000 items organically over the years
